name: INTRATE
description: INTRATE returns the simple annual interest rate for a security that is purchased at a discount and redeemed at par.
tldr: Calculates the interest rate for a fully invested security.

basicExample.description: Interest rate for a short-term investment
basicExample.explanation: Investing $95,000 and receiving $100,000 after one year implies a simple annual interest rate of about 5.41%.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/365 basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 3 uses actual days and a 365-day year.

howItWorks: INTRATE calculates the simple interest rate using the formula (redemption - investment) / investment * (days per year / days to maturity). It is used for short-term discount instruments.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Investment and redemption are absolute amounts, not per $100.

commonErrors.fix: Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: INTRATE works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between INTRATE and DISC?
faq.answer: INTRATE is based on the investment amount. DISC is based on the redemption value.

faq.question: When is INTRATE used?
faq.answer: It is used for fully invested short-term securities.
